$comment: Artifact vocabulary for the operational-process corpus (founder depth wave part 2, 2026-10-01): the canonical business artifacts that flow between processes. Each artifact names its one canonical producer process (producedBy); documented exceptions (a second committed process that genuinely also brings the artifact into existence - the LLC route's EIN, the conversion's re-issued charter paper) live in alsoProducedBy. terminal=true marks artifacts no committed process consumes (filed 83(b)s, the dissolution certificate) - everything else is consumed by at least one other process's requires, and every artifact is produced by a committed step (the producer task carries it in produces, pinned to the node where it comes into existence via producesArtifact). No invented artifacts: the registry is sized from the corpus itself. Optional `documents` (founder 2026-10-06, classic document objects): the open-documents/registry.json ids whose registered template genuinely IS this artifact's form (the filed 83(b)'s IRS Form 15620, the executed SAFE's YC forms) - deliberately sparse, honest absence for everything with no registered template; referential integrity tested in lib/__tests__/processArtifacts.test.ts. Read back by lib/processes.ts loadArtifacts(); the cross-process dependency graph builds in lib/processDeps.ts; schema: schemas/process-artifacts.schema.json.

artifacts.label: Company name
artifacts.description: The chosen company/brand name - picked from ranked candidates checked against domains, social handles, and trademark conflicts. Feeds the incorporation name check, domain search, trademark filing, and brand monitoring.

artifacts.label: Brand logo
artifacts.description: The primary company logo, generated and set for the chosen brand. Used by the website, the trademark filing, launch assets, and the app-store listings.

artifacts.label: Brand color palette
artifacts.description: The brand color palette, contrast-checked and set as design tokens. Consumed when the company website is generated.

artifacts.label: Domain shortlist
artifacts.description: Ranked available domain candidates with pricing and renewal costs, with matching social handles checked. The input to the actual domain purchase.

artifacts.label: Registered domain
artifacts.description: The company's registered domain name. Everything on the company's own address hangs off it: the email workspace, DNS records, the website, email routing, and the status page.

artifacts.label: DNS control
artifacts.description: Working control of the domain's DNS zone (provisioned with SSL at purchase) - the ability to add the TXT, MX, SPF, and CNAME records that domain verification, email sending, and routing demand.

artifacts.label: Registered agent
artifacts.description: A designated registered agent in the state of incorporation - the legal-documents recipient every state filing names, required before the incorporation filing itself.

artifacts.label: Certificate of Incorporation
artifacts.description: The state-stamped Certificate of Incorporation - proof the C-Corp exists. The EIN application, bank KYC, state registrations, annual filings, the data room, and ultimately the dissolution all consume it.

artifacts.label: Bylaws & initial board consent
artifacts.description: The signed bylaws and initial board consent - the company's internal operating rules and first corporate act. A charter document every diligence data room carries.

artifacts.label: Founder stock issuance
artifacts.description: The signed founder stock purchase agreements - the founders' shares as issued paper. The founding shares entered when the cap table is first set up.

artifacts.label: Filed 83(b) election
artifacts.description: The 83(b) election as filed with the IRS within the 30-day window. A terminal tax artifact: nothing downstream consumes it, but the missed window never reopens.

artifacts.label: LLC Certificate of Formation
artifacts.description: The stamped Certificate of Formation (Articles of Organization accepted) - proof the LLC exists. Consumed when the LLC later converts to a C-Corp.

artifacts.label: LLC operating agreement
artifacts.description: The signed LLC operating agreement governing the members. The members' consent to a later C-Corp conversion runs under it.

artifacts.label: Founder agreement & IP assignment
artifacts.description: The signed founder agreements with IP assignment - the equity split and vesting on paper. Consumed by the cap-table audit and by accelerator applications that ask who owns what.

artifacts.label: EIN
artifacts.description: The company's federal Employer Identification Number from the IRS. Bank accounts, payroll, state tax registrations, payment processors, insurance applications, and the federal return all require it.

artifacts.label: Business mailing address
artifacts.description: The company's business mailing address (virtual mailbox with the notarized USPS 1583 done). Insurance applications and other provider KYC ask for it.

artifacts.label: Business bank account
artifacts.description: The company's business checking account. The money rail every finance process reads or moves: runway, bill pay, wires, bookkeeping, payroll funding, and the raise's incoming wires.

artifacts.label: Corporate card
artifacts.description: The corporate card program for company spend, synced into the books. Expense management configures its per-employee limits.

artifacts.label: Accounting ledger
artifacts.description: The configured accounting system - chart of accounts with bank and card feeds connected. The books every close, report, budget, and tax filing read.

artifacts.label: Financial statements
artifacts.description: The closed-books P&L and balance sheet from the monthly close. The 409A, the data room, the federal return, and the annual budget consume them.

artifacts.label: Cap table
artifacts.description: The live capitalization table - founding shares, SAFEs, and grants recorded. Read by the 409A, option grants, the data room, the raise, the SAFE conversion, franchise tax, and the pre-raise audit.

artifacts.label: Payment processor account
artifacts.description: The activated payment processor account with API keys integrated and payouts confirmed. Billing, invoicing, refunds, revenue reporting, promo codes, and the sales-tax nexus study all run through it.

artifacts.label: Subscription billing
artifacts.description: Configured subscription plans, customer portal, webhooks, and dunning on the payment processor. Pricing changes, churn saves, and win-back campaigns operate on it.

artifacts.label: State tax accounts
artifacts.description: The state tax registration numbers (income, employment, sales where applicable) in operating states. Payroll setup files employment taxes against them.

artifacts.label: Sales tax registrations
artifacts.description: Registrations with each state's department of revenue where nexus thresholds are crossed, with collection and automated filings enabled. Terminal: the platform remits on schedule.

artifacts.label: Foreign qualifications
artifacts.description: Foreign-qualification filings in states with employees or offices. Withdrawn one by one when the company shuts down.

artifacts.label: Insurance policies
artifacts.description: Bound D&O, E&O, general liability, and cyber coverage. The office lease's certificate-of-insurance requirement draws on it.

artifacts.label: Federal tax return
artifacts.description: The filed federal corporate return (Form 1120). The R&D credit's Form 6765 rides on it.

artifacts.label: Certificate of dissolution
artifacts.description: The accepted certificate of dissolution - the company's legal end. Terminal by definition.

artifacts.label: Privacy policy
artifacts.description: The published privacy policy (and DPA flow) on the company site. Security questionnaires and app-store privacy labels point at it.

artifacts.label: Terms of Service
artifacts.description: The drafted and counsel-reviewed Terms of Service published to the website. Terminal: customers accept it; no committed process consumes it downstream.

artifacts.label: SaaS agreement template
artifacts.description: The standard SaaS subscription agreement template, counsel-reviewed. The SLA's credit terms get added into it.

artifacts.label: Executed NDA
artifacts.description: A countersigned mutual NDA, filed. Terminal: event paper for one counterparty.

artifacts.label: IP assignments (PIIA)
artifacts.description: Executed proprietary-information and invention-assignment agreements for every founder and employee. Diligence data rooms must carry them.

artifacts.label: Trademark application
artifacts.description: The USPTO trademark application and its serial number, as filed. Terminal: prosecution runs at the USPTO's pace.

artifacts.label: Signed board minutes
artifacts.description: Signed board minutes filed on cadence - the clean corporate record a priced round's diligence reads.

artifacts.label: Board-approved annual budget
artifacts.description: The operating plan and headcount budget the board signed off. Terminal: departments execute against it.

artifacts.label: Company email workspace
artifacts.description: The company email/calendar/docs workspace on the domain. Sending company mail, provisioning hires, routing aliases, the CRM inbox, outbound sequences, and SSO identity all build on it.

artifacts.label: Team chat workspace
artifacts.description: The team chat workspace with default channels. Hiring, offboarding, alerts, approvals, and announcements all land in it.

artifacts.label: Project tracker
artifacts.description: The configured project tracker (teams, workflows, labels). Issues, projects, incident follow-ups, pen-test findings, and OKR key results live in it.

artifacts.label: Team wiki
artifacts.description: The team wiki with meeting notes and process templates. Hypothesis docs, the handbook, board rooms, process docs, and OKR tracking get published into it.

artifacts.label: Document storage
artifacts.description: The shared company document system with its folder structure. The diligence data room is hosted out of it.

artifacts.label: Team password manager
artifacts.description: The team password manager with shared vaults and access groups. Terminal: shared credentials live in it operationally.

artifacts.label: Identity provider (SSO)
artifacts.description: The SSO identity provider tenant with role-based groups and MFA. Hire provisioning (SSO/SCIM), SOC 2 integrations, and quarterly access reviews run through it.

artifacts.label: Device management (MDM)
artifacts.description: The MDM with the fleet enrolled and baseline policies pushed. Terminal: its compliance reports feed SOC 2 evidence continuously.

artifacts.label: Code hosting organization
artifacts.description: The code hosting org with repos, branch protection, and team access. CI, the shipping loop, releases, agent-readiness work, and offboarding's access removal depend on it.

artifacts.label: CI/CD pipeline
artifacts.description: The CI/CD pipeline with test, lint, and deploy jobs. Every feature merge and release cut ships through it.

artifacts.label: Cloud infrastructure
artifacts.description: The production cloud footprint - networking, database, compute, IAM, monitoring. Data-warehouse pipelines and pen-test environments are provisioned from it.

artifacts.label: Company website
artifacts.description: The published company website. Policies, content, pricing pages, signup forms, support widgets, and the careers page all live on it.

artifacts.label: Error tracking
artifacts.description: Error monitoring with alert rules and release tracking wired to the repo. Release monitoring and on-call alerting consume it.

artifacts.label: Product analytics
artifacts.description: Product analytics with the SDK installed and key events defined. Launch spikes, referral conversion, churn saves, and warehouse event sources read from it.

artifacts.label: Incident platform
artifacts.description: On-call schedules, escalation policies, and incident workflows. Postmortems assemble their timelines from it.

artifacts.label: Status page
artifacts.description: The public status page on the company domain with uptime monitors wired. Postmortem write-ups publish to it.

artifacts.label: Data warehouse & BI
artifacts.description: The data warehouse with pipelines from production systems and BI dashboards. Terminal: reporting reads it operationally.

artifacts.label: CRM
artifacts.description: The CRM with pipeline, properties, and the email inbox connected. Outbound lists, health scores, and win-back logging live in it.

artifacts.label: Transactional email
artifacts.description: The transactional email account with the sending domain authenticated. Terminal: the product sends receipts and resets through it.

artifacts.label: Marketing email audience
artifacts.description: The email marketing audience with templates and welcome automation. Referral announcements and win-back sequences send to it.

artifacts.label: Customer support desk
artifacts.description: The support platform with messenger widget, inbox routing, and help center. Terminal: customer conversations flow through it operationally.

artifacts.label: Diligence data room
artifacts.description: The permissioned investor data room - charter docs, cap table, financials, contracts, kept current. Board minutes file into it; the priced round's diligence runs on it.

artifacts.label: Executed SAFEs
artifacts.description: Signed SAFE notes with wires verified - the pre-seed on paper. Cap-table updates, the pre-raise audit, and the priced-round conversion consume them.

artifacts.label: Priced round closing
artifacts.description: The closed priced round - consents signed, closing packet executed, wires verified, shares issued. The trigger for every outstanding SAFE's conversion.

artifacts.label: 409A valuation
artifacts.description: The accepted 409A fair-market-value report. Every option grant - including the first hire's - requires a current one.

artifacts.label: Option grants
artifacts.description: Board-approved, signed, and recorded stock option grants. Offboarding's exercise-window notice runs against them.

artifacts.label: Signed offer / employment agreement
artifacts.description: The accepted offer letter - an employee on paper. Payroll runs, provisioning, reviews, and offboarding all presuppose it.

artifacts.label: Contractor record (W-9 on file)
artifacts.description: A payable 1099 contractor in payroll - W-9 and payment details on file. Year-end 1099 filings verify against it.

artifacts.label: Payroll account
artifacts.description: The configured payroll provider - the system of record for paying people and filing employment taxes. Hiring, payroll runs, contractors, the 401(k), visa updates, R&D payroll offset, and the final payroll all run on it.

artifacts.label: Benefits plan
artifacts.description: The company's enrolled benefits (health, dental, vision) configured in payroll. New-hire enrollment and offboarding termination act on it.

artifacts.label: 401(k) plan
artifacts.description: The adopted retirement plan with the payroll integration connected. Terminal: contributions sync on every payroll run.

artifacts.label: Applicant tracking system
artifacts.description: The ATS with interview stages, postings, and scorecards. The multi-role hiring pipeline is built on top of it.

artifacts.label: Employee handbook
artifacts.description: The published employee handbook - policies, PTO, conduct, remote work, equity. Terminal: the team works under it.

artifacts.label: Office lease
artifacts.description: The signed office lease with deposit wired and certificate of insurance delivered. Terminal: the company occupies under it.

artifacts.label: Compliance platform
artifacts.description: The compliance automation platform with integrations connected. MDM evidence, vendor reviews, and the Type II's continuous monitoring wire into it.

artifacts.label: Security policies
artifacts.description: The reviewed security policy set generated for SOC 2. The policy corpus security questionnaires are answered from.

artifacts.label: SOC 2 Type I report
artifacts.description: The completed SOC 2 Type I audit - the point-in-time snapshot the Type II observation window starts from.

artifacts.label: SOC 2 Type II report
artifacts.description: The SOC 2 Type II report published to the trust center. Terminal: enterprise buyers read it.

artifacts.label: Pen test report & attestation
artifacts.description: The annual penetration test report with retest attestation letter. SOC 2 Type II fieldwork expects it.

artifacts.label: Vendor contract
artifacts.description: A signed vendor agreement from the selection process. Vendor security reviews assess them; shutdown cancels them.

artifacts.label: Fund LP certificate
artifacts.description: The stamped Delaware Certificate of Limited Partnership - the fund vehicle exists. The close runs on it.

artifacts.label: Fund LPA & GP operating agreement
artifacts.description: The signed limited partnership agreement and GP operating agreement. Subscription documents and the close execute under them (amended & restated at close).

artifacts.label: Fund bank account
artifacts.description: The fund's own bank account. Closing wires and capital calls land in it.

artifacts.label: Fund closing
artifacts.description: The held first-and-final close - LP subscriptions signed and the A&R LPA executed with the final LP schedule. Capital calls only exist after it.
